gen-gf-revalia-gf-hind-guntur: The lowercase g in Revalia leaves its lower curve open, setting a bold, loosely spaced stride across the line. And Hind Guntur, with no thick-thin shift anywhere, gives that showy heading a sturdy, modern partner.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-hind-madurai: Revalia's open-bottomed g and widely separated letters give the heading a loose, bold stride before the text begins. Hind Madurai settles beneath it with a stroke weight that never varies.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-hind-mysuru: Revalia's g leaves its lower curve open, and the widely separated letters stroll along with bold, relaxed confidence. Hind Mysuru, a contemporary sans with pencil-like lines, would read smoothly paragraph after paragraph.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-hind-siliguri: Revalia leaves its g open at the bottom and swaggers wide. Hind Siliguri, a sans with a flat, constant line weight, hums quietly below, leaving the heading to do the shouting.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-hind-vadodara: Hind Vadodara reads wide-mouthed and tidy, a sans-serif with tall bowls. Beside it, Revalia feels louder and looser, its open-tailed g and widely separated letters making the text look disciplined.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-huninn: Huninn is a modern sans-serif with sturdy, uniform strokes. Revalia is best at making noise, with its open-curled g and loosely spaced letters, while Huninn is best at staying out of the way.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-inter-tight: Expressive from the first letter, Revalia leaves its g open. Where Revalia grabs attention, Inter Tight, a modern sans with short ascenders and drawn-back curve tails, does the quiet work of carrying the words.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-karla: Revalia is the showpiece here, a bold display face whose g keeps its lower curve open and whose letters stand apart. Revalia grabs the eye; Karla, stocky and sans-serif, does the talking.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-kedebideri: Kedebideri reads tall and friendly, its rounded letters staying open. Below the bold, widely spaced Revalia heading, that sans text settles in, while the open-curved g adds a bit of swagger.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-khula: Khula reads full-bodied, with a tall middle and open curves. What stands out is the gap in temperament: Revalia is bold and widely spaced with an open g, while the sans Khula stays modest and neutral.
